name: Afamelanotide
used_for: FDA-labeled (Scenesse) to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with a history of phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP). It is a melanocortin 1 receptor agonist supplied as a subcutaneous implant, not an injection, placed by a trained health care professional. It has no FDA-approved use for tanning; products sold online as melanotan are not the approved implant.

entries.text: Labeled dosing: a single 16 mg implant inserted subcutaneously above the anterior supra-iliac crest by a trained health care professional every 2 months, using the supplied cannula. The label says to maintain sun and light protection measures during treatment.
entries.population: Adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) per the Scenesse label

administration_guidance.text: The label states the implant is placed under the skin above the anterior supra-iliac crest by a trained healthcare professional, about every 2 months, using a dedicated implantation cannula.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label states sun and light protection measures are to be maintained during treatment to prevent phototoxic reactions related to erythropoietic protoporphyria.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label states storage in a refrigerator at 2 to 8 C (36 to 46 F), protected from light.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label states the patient is placed in a comfortable reclined supine position before the insertion site is identified, and is monitored for 30 minutes after the implant is placed.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The label states the implant is resorbable and may not be locatable from about 10 days after insertion, which makes removal difficult after that time.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: The most common adverse reactions in the label's trials were implant site reaction (21% versus 10% with vehicle), nausea (19% versus 14%), oropharyngeal pain (7% versus 5%), cough (6% versus 3%) and fatigue (6% versus 3%).
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Skin hyperpigmentation occurred in 4% versus 0% with vehicle. The label warns of generalized increased pigmentation and darkening of existing nevi (moles), with full body skin examination twice yearly.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The label warns that serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: A Superpower guide says afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, has no approved cosmetic tanning indication, can darken moles, and that online 'Melanotan I' products are not the pharmaceutical-grade implant. The company says it does not sell or prescribe the drug.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Scenesse (afamelanotide) implant (Clinuvel), published May 2026.
research.finding: Approved to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with EPP; one 16 mg implant every 2 months; warnings for hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis) and darkening of moles, with twice-yearly skin exams advised.

research.summary: Two randomized placebo-controlled trials (US and EU) of afamelanotide implants in people with erythropoietic protoporphyria (Langendonk et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Median pain-free time in sunlight was 69.4 vs 40.8 hours (US, 6 months) and 6.0 vs 0.8 hours (EU, 9 months); phototoxic reactions were fewer in the EU trial; quality of life improved. Adverse events were mostly mild. Funded by the manufacturer and others.
